props.covers: The live canvas-agent session lifecycle: scope resolution, draft page-frame injection, per-run boot perception, the sixteen-tool runtime, typed-operation lowering, tiered operation results, painted-extent cameras, static rendering, finalize gates, and the proposal handoff to the studio.

text.insert: Agent kernel architecture

The kernel hosts a scoped, draft-based canvas editing session. The model begins with a current textual and visual snapshot, edits the draft through typed single-operation mutators, uses a deliberate look for whole-board truth, and can finish only by proposing a cumulative document diff or ending without a proposal.

The saved canvas document is the baseline and the session draft is the working truth. Geometry, containment, routing, diagnostics, and renders are recomputed from documents; the model never edits an intermediate layout representation. The operator remains the authority that accepts or rejects a proposal.
Session lifecycle

createSession validates the canvas id, a non-empty selection, and a non-empty instruction; reads the saved canvas as the baseline; hashes it for later accept-time checks; and resolves the selected ids through
board/scope.ts
. Selecting a section includes its stored descendants. The resolution records the exact in-scope object ids, their bounding frame, and the number of connections crossing the scope boundary.

createSession
  → read + hash baseline
  → resolve selected object ids
  → create draft and inject a page frame when needed
  → merge annotations into the request queue
  → boot current text context + images
  → run model against the sixteen tools
  → proposal-ready | abandoned | error
  → operator accepts or rejects a proposal
Before the run starts,
draftWithPageFrame

ensures the draft has a root section locked as background. If the saved document has no such frame, the harness derives one from the document size or object bounds, gives it the conventional id page-frame when available, and inserts it into the draft. The frame is the page boundary. No section resizes itself, and the page frame cannot be removed through the model surface; like any section, it can be resized or fitted on request.
Per-run boot perception
Every run, including a refinement in an existing model session, recomputes perception from the current draft.
bootPerception

pairs board-state text with three boot images: a painted-extent full-board render, the house-style exemplar, and the vocabulary contact sheet. The exemplar and contact-sheet results are cached after their first process-local render attempts. A board-render failure is noted in board_state, and unavailable images are omitted rather than failing the spawn.
The context sidecar's
assembleImages

hook delivers the current board PNG first, the exemplar PNG second, and the vocabulary contact-sheet PNG third. The contact sheet renders and labels every object type, every icon glyph, every color, and connection demonstrations including a wire that ends on a section. Missing image payloads are omitted without changing the tagged text blocks.

The system prompt has four top-level sections: purpose, board_model, state_grammar, and workflow. Workflow contains six nested phase blocks—understand, survey, plan, build, finish, and finalize—and each phase carries objective, steps, and constraints. There is no separate rules section; phase constraints own those requirements. Build is sections-first: the section skeleton goes down first, content fills one section at a time with each render judged, a finished region closes with fit_section, then connections, labels, and styling follow.

Five tagged blocks form the boot text, with every child line indented four spaces: editor_state describes the instruction, baseline, selection, resolved scope frame, boundary-edge count, and optional viewport; user_requests is the status-bearing annotation queue; capabilities nests sections, stickies, objects, and connections, each with description, ops, named functionality topics, generated vocabulary or fields where applicable, and tips; style_guide contains the single nested aesthetic topic; and board_state contains the full, untruncated board digest followed by the current lint report. The object roster lists bare type names so the agent chooses geometry; icon glyphs and colors are enumerated one per line. During editing, look is the authoritative whole-board recall affordance.
The sixteen-tool runtime

The model has exactly sixteen tools. Sections, stickies, objects, and connections each expose add, update, and remove mutators; fit_section completes the thirteen mutators built from one shared operation factory. look, resolve_request, and finalize complete the surface. Their kernel declarations live in
agent/catalog/layout-editor/tools.ts
; their session-bound implementations live in
service/session/tools.ts

. The session tools retain request disposal and finalization. The runtime looks up the current layout session from the kernel run context, and every mutator carries the same optional view and declares sequential execution so call order is guaranteed.

Each typed mutator names exactly one operation and accepts its operation-specific fields plus the shared optional view. One call applies one edit. look({ view? }) is the separate read-only perception call: it judges the full board and adds a named-section close-up when view is supplied.

resolve_request({ id, status, note }) disposes one open queue entry as done or declined. The note is required and the response is the updated REQUESTS block only. Queue entries retain their stable R-number and do not disappear merely because an annotation is removed from the draft.

finalize({ outcome, message }) is terminal on success. outcome committed builds a proposal for operator review after rechecking its gates. outcome none marks the session abandoned, emits the abandonment reason, and ends without a proposal. A rejected finalize call leaves the run active so the model can correct the draft or queue.
Model operations and the studio wire
The model surface is declaration-style and kind-specific. The classification seam in
op-surface.ts
renders the six-kind grammar in the model's terms; thirteen operation specs own per-operation state validation, and OpContext owns lowering to that grammar.

sections     add_section · update_section · remove_section
stickies     add_sticky · update_sticky · remove_sticky
objects      add_object · update_object · remove_object
connections  add_connection · update_connection · remove_connection
layout       fit_section

Section and sticky operations imply their entity type and reject a type field on add. Object operations accept only the generated object-type roster, excluding section and sticky. Update and remove operations verify that the target is the expected kind; a wrong-kind target produces a steering error naming the correct operation family.

The tool schema catches field presence, types, enums, id format, and complete {x, y, width, height} geometry before execute runs. Per-operation state validation checks existence, entity kind, and board invariants; failures return error lines only, with no mutation, perception, or event. Non-fatal observations appear as notes under APPLIED. Duplicate ids, self-loops, and missing targets are validation errors; a duplicate edge over an existing from→to pair applies with a warning, and an empty fit is a no-op. A connection endpoint must already exist on the draft, and the validation error names its field, so objects go down before the edge that joins them. An operation applies or it does not: atomicity belongs to the call, not to validator orchestration.

remove_section rejects a locked background frame. When applied to another section, removal cascades through its descendants, their incident connections, and annotations that target removed objects or connections. Object and sticky removal likewise clears incident connections.

The operation context maps section and sticky adds, updates, and removals onto addObject, updateObject, and removeObject with the appropriate implied type. Object and connection operations pass through. classifyOperation performs the inverse classification when cumulative diffs are rendered back in the model's grammar.

Below this boundary, the canvas and studio continue to speak the six CanvasAgentPatchOperation kinds: add, update, and remove for objects and connections. Sections and stickies are ordinary objects on that wire. Keeping the six-operation wire means the draft applier, document differ, studio accept path, and canvas reducer share one mechanical format while the model receives safer kind-specific steering.
The proposal wire is always rebuilt from baseline and draft.
diffDocuments

emits the ordered internal six-operation list. Derived parentId membership and read-only annotations are omitted so the live canvas can derive or keep them; endpoint anchors, endpoint positions, and waypoints are stored connection fields — agent steering, not derived routing — and are diffed and carried in the proposal.
Operation results and deliberate perception

Before execute, the runtime validates the tool schema. The shared factory then resolves the session and snapshots its draft; a state-validation failure returns ERROR with no mutation, perception, or event. The apply stage can return a no-op note and stop. A changing call reconciles membership from geometry, derives DELTA and the lint delta, reports routes for a touched connection, renders only when view was supplied, prints the request queue, and emits one run-UX event. Adds start with parentId null and object updates strip parentId because containment derives from geometry.

fit_section reads the named frame's children from a membership-reconciled draft, computes the fitted geometry, and lands it as an ordinary geometry update on that one section. No ancestor is touched: fitting is a finishing move, and a cascade would compress a parent around whichever children happen to exist. A childless section returns a no-op note. Because the result lowers to a plain section geometry patch, nothing below the lowering line needs a special case.

The factory derives DELTA by comparing the before and after documents rather than echoing the call. Consequently it reports direct edits together with 16px-snapped or fitted geometry, reconciled parentId, endpoint reassignment, anchors, endpoint positions, and waypoint changes. The APPLIED line names the operation, and any non-fatal observations follow as notes.

look is the only full-board perception result. It returns a fresh BOARD digest, the cumulative baseline-to-draft BOARD DIFF rendered from the same diffDocuments operations that a committed finalize proposes, the complete lint list in prose, routed truth, and the full request queue. It also carries a 1600px full-board render and, when view is supplied, a 1400px close-up of that section.

Every mutator returns one of three result classes, distinguished by headline. APPLIED · <tool> <id> carries the document-derived DELTA, lint delta, a digest scoped to the touched section, routed truth for a touched connection, the request queue, an optional full-board PNG when view was supplied, and one run-UX event. NO-OP · <tool> <id> — <note> carries the note only; ERROR · <tool> — <lines> carries the error lines only. Both leave the draft untouched and emit no event. Raster failures are written into the result text rather than silently dropping an expected image.
Painted-extent camera contract

paintedBounds measures what the renderer paints, not just object rectangles. Its union includes object geometry, icon caption bands, section title chips, production-routed connection polylines, and connection label chips. renderBoardView frames the full painted union with padding and then expands to fit section title chips at the view's effective zoom.

renderSectionView frames the named section, its descendants, and fully internal connections. It retains every object or connection whose painted extent intersects the camera and retains the true endpoint objects needed to route those connections. A connection crossing the section boundary is drawn to the frame edge and visibly clipped by the SVG viewBox; it is never dropped. Routing always uses the whole document as the obstacle set, so a camera does not change the route.

Section title chips follow the live stage's counter-scale curve: max((1/zoom)^0.6, 1), capped at 6. The camera performs a bounded fixed-point fit because chip size depends on camera zoom. Connection label chips remain fixed world geometry and do not scale. These rules are implemented in
@codecaine-ai/canvas/render
, which is the session harness's only named-view seam.
Static rendering and raster safety

The static renderer emits deterministic, self-contained SVG without React, DOM APIs, external styles, or foreignObject. It uses the production connector router, the canvas palette and stroke rules, the same text slots as the live stage, and true silhouettes for document, database, folder, document-stack, cylinder-horizontal, internal-storage, page-corner, and predefined-process.

Text wrapping and ellipsis use generated Inter advance tables for the regular and true wght-700 instances. Sticky notes are laid out from the same markdown parser into matching heading, bullet, bold, code, indentation, and line-box structure. The harness rasterizes SVG with resvg and bundled Inter. Before entering native code it validates the root viewport, caps raster dimensions, and rejects degenerate or wholly off-viewport nested SVG and filtered elements; the SVG renderer also omits rasterizer-unsafe features from off-camera elements.
Finalize gates and proposal handoff

A committed finalize runs the finishing registry—the five always-on diagnostics plus frame-slack, which asks whether a frame is far larger than its children need—then filters them to the baseline scope plus draft-created objects. Any error-tier finding in that edited scope blocks finalization. Warnings do not block; unresolved scoped warnings are carried in the proposal lint text. Crowding is a warning-tier corridor floor for sibling nodes: 80px side by side and 48px stacked. Both are the clearance a routed wire and its chip physically need, not a preferred gap; stacked peers sit closer because a wire between them usually runs along the gap rather than across it.

Every request must also be done or declined. Open queue entries block finalization beside error diagnostics. If the draft matches the baseline and no proposal already exists, there is nothing to propose and the committed finalize is rejected.

On pass, finalize calls diffDocuments, stores the resulting six-operation patch with the model's summary and warning report, sets the session status to proposal-ready, and emits the proposal-ready event. outcome none sets status abandoned and emits the abandoned event. Those event names and proposal operation shapes are the stable service-to-studio wire.

Accept re-reads the saved canvas. If the baseline hash still matches, the store returns the proposal's CanvasAgentPatchOperation array to the studio. If the file changed, accept permits the handoff only when every baseline-scoped object still exists with the same geometry; otherwise it returns a conflict and the operator must run against the current board. Reject marks the session rejected without returning a patch.
